description: The figure contains two side-by-side vertical bar charts illustrating inter-annotator agreement (Fleiss Kappa) as a function of two sample-level ambiguity measures: ambiguity standard deviation (left) and maximum ambiguity (right). In both charts, the horizontal axis contains the category values (left labeled “Ambiguity Std” with categories 0.0, 0.47, 0.82, 0.94 in that left-to-right order; right labeled “Max Ambiguity” with categories 1, 2, 3 in left-to-right order), and the vertical axis is labeled “Fleiss Kappa” with a linear scale spanning roughly 0.0 to just under 1.0 and tick marks shown at regular intervals (approximately 0.2). In the left chart, four single bars (shaded in blue tones) are shown with numeric annotations above each bar: Ambiguity Std 0.0 has a dark blue bar at about 0.88, 0.47 has a medium blue bar at about 0.46, 0.82 has a light blue bar at about 0.03, and 0.94 has a lighter blue bar at about 0.24. In the right chart, three single bars (also in blue tones) are annotated: Max Ambiguity 1 has a dark blue bar at about 0.89, 2 has a medium blue bar at about 0.46, and 3 has a lighter blue bar at about 0.23. There is no legend, no stacking or grouping within categories beyond one bar per category, the categories appear in ascending numeric order on each x-axis, and the bars are not additionally emphasized beyond the value labels placed above them.
caption_used: Inter-annotator agreement compared to sample-level ambiguity standard deviation and sample-level maximum ambiguity values. The left chart shows Fleiss Kappa values decreasing steadily as Ambiguity Std increases, with values approximately 0.88, 0.46, 0.12, and 0.24 for categories 0.0, 0.47, 0.82, and 0.94, respectively. The right chart demonstrates a similar trend, with Fleiss Kappa values declining from 0.89 to 0.46 and then to 0.12 for Max Ambiguity categories 1, 2, and 3. The data suggests a consistent negative correlation between ambiguity measures and inter-annotator agreement.
